rank1.why: the frozen root authority itself was structurally valid. Each item ran from a STRUCTURALLY_VALID website claim, the root-authority contract was satisfied, and a fetch observation was written - which the gateway can only do once a root authority has been established

rank2.why: no readable or evaluable robots policy explicitly disallowed the crawl. robots_decision is NOT_APPLICABLE on the single observation, which is the value pinned to the request that RETRIEVES the policy file. The policy was never read, so nothing in it could disallow anything

why: DNS resolution SUCCEEDED - the hostname resolved and addresses were returned
the returned addresses were deliberately refused by the landed non-public-address safety guard
BLOCKED_BY_POLICY is not one of the frozen rank-3 failure classes
this was an intentional policy refusal before transport, not a DNS, TLS, connect or read transport failure
rank3.note: rank 3's clause 'where no usable HTTP response established an application-level page outcome' is a QUALIFIER on its enumerated failures, not an independent sufficient condition. Reading it as sufficient would make rank 3 swallow every response-less failure and would empty rank 4 of the fallback role its own text gives it

rank4.why: rank 4 is explicitly the fallback mechanical reason for EVERY remaining determinate SD9 failure with formal post-SD7 count < 4 to which ranks 1-3 do not apply. Both items are determinate (range [0,0], exact), both are below 4, and ranks 1-3 have each been excluded on the frozen text

previousInterpretiveConcernNotCarriedFor.reasonNotCarriedForward: adding an unstated HTTP-response condition to rank 4 would revise the taxonomy by reading, which this decision explicitly refuses to do.
